w: This Plumstead pitch was home to Royal Arsenal, the football club that came to be known as Woolwich Arsenal and, eventually, simply Arsenal. Long before the trophies and the global stardom, one of England's most famous clubs took some of its earliest steps on this south-east London ground.
s: Birthplace ground of the club now known as Arsenal FC
_facts: Former football stadium in Plumstead, south-east London
Home ground of Royal Arsenal FC
Club later renamed Woolwich Arsenal, then Arsenal FC

w: Opened in 1925 between Welling and Bexleyheath, this 75-hectare park is the second-largest in the borough of Bexley, after Foots Cray Meadows, and its most used green space. Grade II listed on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens, it lends its name to the electoral ward that surrounds it.
s: 75-hectare Grade II park between Welling and Bexleyheath
_facts: Opened in 1925
75 hectares; second-largest park in the borough of Bexley
Grade II listed on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens
Gives its name to the surrounding electoral ward

w: Its nave, chancel and apse date to the first half of the 12th century, and it is claimed to be the oldest parish church still in weekly use in Greater London -- Grade I listed. A white marble font given in 1639, faint 13th-century wall paintings, and the unmarked grave of antiquarian William Stukeley all survive here.
s: Possibly London's oldest parish church still in weekly use
_facts: Nave, chancel and apse date to the early 12th century
Grade I listed; claimed oldest parish church in weekly use in Greater London
1639 white marble font given by Sir Richard Heigham
Antiquarian William Stukeley is buried in the churchyard, without a monument

w: At its peak this garrison commanded two division headquarters and around seven battalions. The Royal Artillery Barracks stayed the Royal Artillery's headquarters until 2007, when it moved to Larkhill; the army itself is due to leave Woolwich in 2028, though the King's Troop, Royal Horse Artillery, will remain.
s: Home of the Royal Artillery until 2007, army leaving by 2028
_facts: At its largest oversaw two division HQs and about seven battalions
Headquarters of the Royal Artillery until 2007, then moved to Larkhill
Army scheduled to leave Woolwich in 2028
King's Troop, Royal Horse Artillery, will remain

w: Built largely within the shell of the 1990s Millennium Dome, the O2 now holds an arena, a music club, a cinema, a bowling alley and a guided climb over the roof to a viewing platform. Locals still just call it the Dome -- its huge canopy survived the Millennium Experience's closure while everything beneath it was completely rebuilt.
s: The old Millennium Dome, reborn as an entertainment district
_facts: Built largely within the former Millennium Dome
Includes an arena, music club, cinema, bowling alley and guided rooftop tour
Renamed The O2 in 2005 after naming rights were sold
The Dome's shell remained while the interior was completely redeveloped

w: Two months after this 22-storey tower opened in 1968, a gas explosion blew out load-bearing walls and one entire corner collapsed, killing four people and injuring seventeen. The disaster exposed flaws in both design and construction, and triggered sweeping changes to British building regulations for high-rise housing.
s: Gas-blast collapse that rewrote UK building regulations
_facts: 22-storey tower block in Canning Town, opened 1968
Partial collapse two months after opening, 16 May 1968
Caused by a gas explosion blowing out load-bearing walls
Four killed, 17 injured; led to major changes in UK building regulations
